text:
maria: Heads-up — ap-east dedicated pools showing CPU and p99 token-latency spikes during tenant microbursts. Looks like slot fragmentation + egress queuing when small tenants suddenly submit lots of short requests :thinking_face:
kevin: Can you paste the shorttrace or SLO window?
maria: p99 tok latency jumps from 45ms -> 420ms for ~3m every hour. node-level CPU OK, but gpu_util jumps and we see long wait in our scheduler queues. Also seeing net_tx_q_depth climb on a subset of nodes.
devon: That sounds like lots of tiny sessions creating KV cache churn + NIC queue saturation. Are those tenants running many parallel hot-starts?
maria: Exactly. Many 1-2s gen calls that pin a slice and never reuse kv cache; fragmentation means we can't pack newer requests efficiently.
sarah: This is the classic small-tenant 'slot-hog' problem. We've had mitigation ideas: proactive slot scrubbing (compact small slices), or a backpressure routing rule to push tiny, bursty traffic to a pre-warmed ephemeral pool.
kevin: I like backpressure routing but worried about cross-region cost if apac bursts spill into eu-west. We need region-awareness + cost cap.
jamal: Proposal sketch: add a lightweight per-tenant burst_classifier that marks requests as SHORT:tokens<64 && latency_target<200ms. SHORT requests get routed through a "burst fastpath" pool with tighter packing and NIC shaping, and fall back to standard pool when overloaded.
nate: For packing we could implement a slot-scrub job: periodic compaction that consolidates active small sessions onto fewer GPUs during low-util windows (02:00-04:00 local) and frees full slices for larger tenants. That reduces fragmentation long-term.
maria: Agree. Also add egress shaping on burst pool: token throttle + cwnd cap per-tenant to avoid net_tx_q blowups.
kevin: How intrusive is the routing change? Can we do it as a policy in the proxy layer (no runtime changes)?
devon: Yes — proxy can tag and route to a dedicated burst routing pool. Need CI for model-compat fallback: if a model isn't available in burst pool, fallback to main but with queuing SLO.
sarah: Also add a cheap canary: route 1% of shorts for 24h and monitor p99, tail drops, and egress qdepth. Dashboards: burst_pool.p99, node.net_tx_q_depth, slot_fragmentation_ratio.
jamal: Safety hooks: auto-failover if burst_pool.p99 > 2x baseline or egress drop > 0.5% for 5m. Also billing tag so finance can see cost shift.
maria: Implementation plan:
- Phase 0: instrumentation + dashboards (48h)
- Phase 1: proxy policy + canary (1%) (1 week)
- Phase 2: slot-scrub compactor running 02:00-04:00 (2 weeks)
- Phase 3: scale rollout + automatic auto-tiering (4 weeks)
kevin: Sounds reasonable. Who owns phase 1 canary? I can take proxy rules + canary orchestration.
maria: I'll own slot-scrub compactor design with devon. Jamal you take the classifier + safety hooks. Sarah will own dashboards and alerts. Nate please coordinate maintenance window for compaction.
nate: I'll slack infra-schedule to book 02:00-04:00 ap-east next 3 nights and add the compaction job.
ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary-routing-rule -> canary namespace at 2109876800 (automated) :white_check_mark:
kevin: One more ask — add a per-tenant budget cap to avoid abuse during canary. If a tenant crosses X tokens in the burst pool, eject them for 10m and route to main.
jamal: added to spec. Also will emit metric shortburst.token_count per tenant.
sarah: I'll add dashboard panels and an alert: burst_pool.net_qdepth > 80% for 3m triggers page to infra oncall.
maria: Great. If we see improvement we can generalize rule to dedicated pools in other regions. If it doesn't help, fallback is to tighten tenant admission or expand dedicated capacity.
devon: One caveat: compaction requires live migration of active sessions; we'll implement by draining new allocs off nodes being compacted to avoid preemption of active KV caches.
kevin: OK let's sync tomorrow 10am PT for rollout decisions. Thanks all :thumbsup:
